matched.actualTitle: Padding Oracle Attack on AES-256-CBC Encrypted CAPTCHA Cookies with Hardcoded Key
matched.matchReason: Both findings describe the same vulnerability: padding oracle attacks on AES-CBC encrypted CAPTCHA storage with PKCS7 padding. The actual finding comprehensively covers the expected finding by identifying (1) error message differences that enable padding oracle attacks ('Invalid padding' vs 'Invalid CAPTCHA!' responses), (2) CBC mode susceptibility, (3) the hardcoded encryption key that enables direct decryption, and (4) the same impact of CAPTCHA bypass and unauthorized access. The actual finding provides additional detail by identifying both attack vectors: direct decryption using hardcoded key AND padding oracle exploitation through error distinction.

extra.title: Missing Secure Flag on CAPTCHA Cookie
extra.assessment: Valid new discovery - legitimate security vulnerability. The CAPTCHA cookie lacks Secure, HttpOnly, and SameSite flags, making it vulnerable to MITM attacks, XSS theft, and CSRF attacks. This is a distinct cookie security issue separate from the padding oracle vulnerability.

extra.title: Missing Secure and SameSite Flags on Session Cookie
extra.assessment: Valid new discovery - legitimate security vulnerability. Session cookie lacks Secure flag and SameSite attribute despite having HttpOnly flag. Creates MITM and CSRF attack vectors against authenticated sessions.

extra.title: Missing Security Response Headers (CSP, X-Frame-Options, X-Content-Type-Options, X-XSS-Protection, HSTS)
extra.assessment: Valid new discovery - legitimate security vulnerability. Application lacks critical defense-in-depth security headers that protect against clickjacking, MIME sniffing, XSS, and SSL stripping attacks. Standard security hygiene finding.

extra.title: Hardcoded AES-256 Encryption Key in Application Configuration
extra.assessment: Valid new discovery - legitimate critical vulnerability. While this is mentioned as a contributing factor in the padding oracle finding, it deserves separate identification as a critical cryptographic key management failure. The hardcoded key 'CCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCC' enables immediate decryption of all CAPTCHA values without requiring padding oracle exploitation.

extra.title: CSRF Token Validation - Improper Error Handling (500 Internal Server Error)
extra.assessment: Valid new discovery - legitimate security vulnerability. CSRF validation failures return HTTP 500 instead of appropriate 4xx status codes, leaking information about validation pipeline and creating information disclosure vulnerability distinct from CSRF bypass.

extra.title: Missing CSRF Token Validation - Requests Pass Through Without Valid Token
extra.assessment: Valid new discovery - legitimate critical vulnerability. CSRF token validation is not properly enforced; requests with missing, empty, or invalid CSRF tokens bypass validation and reach CAPTCHA stage. This is a complete failure of CSRF protection mechanism.

extra.title: CAPTCHA Brute Force Attack - No Rate Limiting on Validation Attempts
extra.assessment: Valid new discovery - legitimate security vulnerability. No rate limiting, exponential backoff, or account lockout implemented on CAPTCHA attempts, allowing exhaustive brute force of CAPTCHA answers within seconds.

extra.title: CAPTCHA Bypass via Empty or Arbitrary String Submission
extra.assessment: Valid new discovery - legitimate critical vulnerability. CAPTCHA validation accepts arbitrary strings without format validation (expected 14-character alphanumeric). When combined with hardcoded encryption key, allows trivial CAPTCHA bypass by encrypting attacker-controlled values and submitting matching plaintext.
